intro

Our downloads and screenshots folders hold our most private documents. Bank statements, lab reports, passwords. You can't send those to a cloud AI. SnapSort is an agent that sorts them using three Gemma models running entirely on this laptop.
backlog
It has already worked through twenty two files. Eleven were handled on their own: renamed, filed, and turned into reminders. Eleven are waiting for me, each with a plain reason.
drop_medical
Let's drop in a real blood test report. Gemma 4 E2B identifies it. Gemma 4 E4B pulls out the test results. Then plain code checks every value against the document before anything happens.
pipeline
For every file, I can see exactly how the pipeline handled it. Each step, which model ran, how long it took, and which checks passed.
vault
Medical records always wait for me. I'll lock this one in the vault. It's now encrypted on disk with a local key, and it can only be viewed when I choose to reveal it.
drop_receipt
Even a coffee receipt gets a second look. It shows part of a card number, so SnapSort offers to lock it away, and asks me first.
inbox
Anything sensitive comes with one clear button. This screenshot shows a WiFi password, so the button says lock in vault. And every action can be undone.
ask
I can also just ask. What's my WiFi password? The answer is blurred because it's a secret, and it cites the file it came from.
export
Bills and payments export to a spreadsheet for any dates. Amounts it couldn't verify against the document are marked.
outro
Offline. Stateful. It recovers from crashes, and it knows when to ask. That's SnapSort.
